statements.text: RBM20 binds TTN (the run's note: TTN pre-mRNA, to regulate its splicing)

statements.note: the binding partner is TTN pre-mRNA; BioLean's TTN node is the gene and its products, so the rel is RBM20 to TTN

statements.text: RBM20 is associated with dilated cardiomyopathy
statements.note: direction none: the source is a title only (one case report, no abstract) and gives no direction for RBM20

evidence.quote: TTN truncating mutations are a common cause of dilated cardiomyopathy

statements.note: direction none: the text gives a direction for truncating variants, not for TTN amount or activity, and says 'Defining the functional effects of TTN truncating mutations should improve our understanding'

evidence.quote: Myosins are actin-based motor molecules with ATPase activity essential for muscle contraction. Forms regular bipolar thick filaments that, together with actin thin filaments, constitute the fundamental contractile unit of skeletal and cardiac muscle

statements.text: MYH7 is associated with dilated cardiomyopathy

excluded.reason: one general line links MYH7 to 'inherited cardiomyopathies' (broader); the background line ('Familial cases ... with sarcomeric gene mutations-particularly in MYH7 and MYBPC3-playing a significant role') is about familial LVNC, the topic of its paragraph, not DCM; the case is one child with DCM/LVNC carrying a MYH7 variant of uncertain significance together with a MYBPC3 VUS, and the MYH7-carrying mother had peripartum cardiomyopathy, not DCM

statements.text: TNNT2 is associated with dilated cardiomyopathy

evidence.quote: a sporadic case of dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) associated with a TNNT2 variant

statements.note: direction none: one likely-pathogenic missense variant (p.Arg104His) in one patient; no direction for TNNT2 amount or activity

statements.text: LMNA is associated with dilated cardiomyopathy (the step's cardiomyocyte context is dropped)

evidence.quote: LMNA R541C variant associated with dilated cardiomyopathy

statements.note: direction none: the text says R541C cardiomyocytes 'exhibited reduced LMNA protein abundance' (prior studies) and that R541C is associated with DCM; joining the two into 'less LMNA goes with DCM' would compose two claims, so it is left unsigned. The context (cell_type Cardiomyocytes) is dropped: it does not limit a gene-disease association to one cell type, it belongs to the note's iPSC-cardiomyocyte finding, and the quote names no cell type. Kind review: the preprint is an iPSC transcriptomic study; the variant's association with DCM is presupposed from prior work, not tested here

unexpressed.reason: LMNA required for the nuclear lamina: the object is a cellular component (GO:0005652), and no target kind holds an effect on a component's integrity or amount

evidence.quote: Lamins are intermediate filament proteins that assemble into a filamentous meshwork, and which constitute the major components of the nuclear lamina

H1.note: the mechanism says 'Disruption of RBM20 alters TTN isoforms ... leading to dilated cardiomyopathy', so RBM20 →− DCM. No claim for TTN: the mechanism gives 'altered TTN isoforms', no direction on TTN.

H2.note: the mechanism: 'Mutations in any of these genes directly disrupt this structural macromolecular complex, impairing overall cardiac contraction and resulting in dilated cardiomyopathy', so each gene →− DCM. The causal part of the chain ends at cardiac muscle contraction (H2.4), which no step links to DCM, so each gene also gets the title's claim 'maintain cardiac contraction' (→+).

H3.note: the mechanism: 'Mutations in LMNA cause a breakdown of the nuclear envelope ... ultimately leading to dilated cardiomyopathy', so LMNA →− DCM. The chain's causal end is the nuclear lamina, a component, which no claim target can hold, so there is no end-node claim.

findings.detail: H1 is three separate edges (an unsigned 'binds' and two unsigned associations), not a chain: the mechanism's causal steps (RBM20 represses TTN exon inclusion, the TTN isoform switch, sarcomere elasticity, DCM) are not steps, so no route can compose.

every H1 step has polarity 'unknown', though the cited UniProt text gives a direction ('Acts as a repressor of mRNA splicing ... leading to the exclusion of specific exons'), and the falsification's expected outcome is also 'unknown', so the test cannot fail.
the step's note says RBM20 binds TTN pre-mRNA, but the object is grounded to the titin protein (UniProtKB:Q8WZ42).
for five canonical DCM genes the gene-disease steps cite 2026 single-case reports or a preprint with zero citations (PMID:41817671 is a title only, no abstract); only TTN (H1.3) cites a cohort study.

PMID:41728227 reports one child with DCM/LVNC carrying a MYH7 VUS plus a MYBPC3 VUS (digenic); the mother carrying the MYH7 variant had peripartum cardiomyopathy, not DCM; it does not state MYH7 is associated with DCM.

the title and mechanism say the three proteins 'physically interact', but the STRING edges cited score experimental 0.00 to 0.11 and database 0.00; the combined scores (0.86 to 0.97) come from text-mining.

the only causal step (MYH7 required for cardiac muscle contraction) ends at contraction, which no step links to DCM; DCM is reached only by unsigned gene-level associations for MYH7 and TNNT2, and never for TTN within H2.
half of H2's steps are unsigned 'binds' edges, so TNNT2 and TTN have no directed path to cardiac contraction or DCM; the physical-interaction premise in the title carries no weight in any arm.
H3.1 ends at the nuclear lamina and H3.2 starts again at LMNA; the mechanism's middle (nuclear envelope breakdown, metabolic and proliferative dysregulation) is only in a note, not in steps.
the cell-type context 'Cardiomyocytes' sits on a gene-disease association step; it belongs to the note's dysregulation finding in iPSC cardiomyocytes, which is not a step.
'Cardiac muscle contraction', 'Nuclear lamina' (kind 'other') and 'Cardiomyocytes' have empty CURIEs though GO:0060048, GO:0005652 and CL:0000746 exist.
a Europe PMC preprint id is cited as 'PMID:PPR1285401'; it is not a PubMed id.

the TTN source also reports 'the rates of cardiac outcomes were similar in subjects with and those without TTN mutations'; no step claims progression, so it refutes nothing here, but contradicting_evidence is empty for every hypothesis.
the run abstained on ABCB9 and OR8J3 ('insufficient_evidence') rather than inventing hypotheses for them.
the abstention cites 'OT:ABCB9-tractability' and 'OT:OR8J3-tractability' for 'Open Targets lacks any disease association scores'; a tractability record does not report disease association.

sources.py does not fetch an abstention's evidence (GWAS:ABCB9:no-association, OT:ABCB9-tractability and the OR8J3 pair are not in sources.json), and the format has no place for a run's 'no association' claim, so the abstention cannot be checked or rendered.
an effect on a cellular component (LMNA required for the nuclear lamina): no target kind takes a component, so the step is unexpressed and the chain's end node cannot be a claim target.

splicing regulation and isoform switching (RBM20 represses TTN exon inclusion) are neither amount nor activity, and protein-RNA binding collapses onto the protein node, so H1's mechanism cannot be written even where the text supports it.

single case reports are recorded as 'observational', the same kind as a cohort or GWAS: the title-only RBM20 case (S2) and the 792-subject TTN NEJM cohort (S3) both get belief 1/2; a case-report kind (or weight) is missing.

one UniProt function line (curatedDb) alone gives belief 4/5 and the verdict 'established', so the only composing arm (MYH7 →+ cardiac muscle contraction) is established on a family-level sentence ('Myosins are ... essential for muscle contraction') with curator-inference code ECO:0000305.

no rule says whether an association direction for a gene may come from a cited variant whose effect on the protein is stated separately (LMNA R541C 'reduced LMNA protein abundance' and is 'associated with dilated cardiomyopathy'); left unsigned.

the TTN evidence is about a variant class (truncating variants) with a clear disease link, but the step is about the gene, so the sharper node (a BLN:TTN-truncating variant) cannot be used without rewriting the step; recorded as an unsigned gene-level association.

the STRING kind rule covers 'experiments or database >= 0.15' and 'only text-mining'; these edges have experimental 0.10 to 0.11 and coexpression 0.15 to 0.47, which neither row covers; recorded as textMined.

the guide does not say whether a run's context field by itself 'limits the result' and so forces a refinement: read literally it turns a gene-disease association with a cell-type context into 'LMNA in cardiomyocytes', a node the LMNA claim cannot reach (it would cut a signed route); the audit dropped the context, as most other runs' curations do for associations.

no cited text states the mechanism's middle: nothing says LMNA mutations cause 'a breakdown of the nuclear envelope in cardiomyocytes' (the preprint reports reduced LMNA protein, sarcomere disorganization and abnormal electrophysiology), and the 'metabolic homeostasis' of the title rests on one variant's (R541C) pathway analysis in iPSC cardiomyocytes, 'dysregulated' with no direction, which the H3.2 note generalises to 'Pathogenic LMNA variants'.

the phenotype-claim rule is for a chain that 'never reaches the disease'; H2's causal step ends at cardiac muscle contraction but the chain still reaches DCM through unsigned gene-level associations, so it is unclear whether the contraction claims (here added, matching the title) are required.

a statement has no field for why an association's direction is none (sign_note is for a derived sign), so the explanations were put in a 'note' key that render.py ignores and the Lean module does not carry; likewise a hypothesis has no per-gene slot for a gene it names but gives no direction for (H1's TTN), so that went in the hypothesis note.

audit.before: subject lmnaInCardiomyocyte (LMNA refined by cellType cardiomyocyte, CL:0000746)
audit.after: subject LMNA; entity lmnaInCardiomyocyte removed; text and note say the context is dropped
audit.reason: the guide drops a qualifier unless it is the point of the step or the context limits the result to it ('muscle and heart only'); a bare cell_type context on a gene-disease association does neither, the curator's own context_misplaced finding says it belongs to the note's iPSC finding, and the kept quote names no cell type, so it did not state the refined claim. The refined node also cut S10 off from H3's LMNA claim and from LMNA ~ DCM statements in other runs.

the quoted span ('LMNA R541C variant associated with dilated cardiomyopathy') is a title clause that presupposes prior clinical work; the preprint itself is an iPSC transcriptomic study and reports no association data, so the span summarises other work.

H3.2's citation is a preprint, not a case report, and its span is now kind review.
